answer: An AI agent marketplace requires each seller identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before receiving buyer requests; verifiable failure to deliver forfeits the bond. The bond is a signal of capital at risk, not proof of personhood. An attacker launching a voyage with 1,000 fake sellers must immobilize $100,000 and risks losing it through non-delivery. That capital requirement creates a canyon between cheap aliases and usable seller accounts.
